open_questions: I2C pads on an OFF face sit above the RP2350-E9 limit. EMU_Fn_SDA/SCL are pulled up through 10 k to Fn_PWR (brief 6.2); with that face off the pad's only path to 0 V is 10 k > 8.2 k, so it can float to ~1.2 V. Harmless (the emulator must not answer for an off face) but it is a FIRMWARE guarantee, not a hardware one: the channel's input buffers must be disabled while EMU_Fn_SENSE reads low. Recorded as firmware rule 2 in the sheet text. A hardware fix would belong on solar_emulation (4.7 k device-side pull-ups, doubling bus current to ~0.7 mA/line) or as 4.7 k pad pull-downs here (which fight the pull-ups when the face is on). I did not change the brief's 10 k.

U202 AP2112K-3.3 (C51118) has no PROVES board precedent - verified live only. The heritage alternative TPS62085RLTT (C2070694) + XFL4015-471MEC (C18221164) is a contained swap in the power block if the hardware lead prefers repo-sourced parts.

ADC_AVDD (U200 pin 44) is tied straight to 3V3_EMU, exactly as the FC ties U18 pin 44 to +3V3, with no ferrite/RC filter. The emulator does not use its ADC in Phase 1 (GPIO26-29 carry digital sense taps). Flag it if Phase 2 wants analogue rail monitoring on those pins.

PIO assumption per critique item 21: one state machine per I2C-slave channel, 7 of the 12 available. If the Phase 3 spike finds a slave needs 2 SMs per channel, 7 channels need 14 and the design breaks. The schematic mitigation already applied without a respin is grouping the four face channels in GPIO0-7 so one PIO block can multiplex them.

UART is on GPIO16/17 because those carry the UART0 TX/RX pin-mux function (no PIO needed). If firmware prefers UART1, GPIO20/21 (EMU_GPIO_SPARE0/1) are the UART1 TX/RX alternates and the map swaps without a respin.

Three global labels appear twice on this sheet (EMU_UART_RX, EMU_GPIO_SPARE0, EMU_GPIO_SPARE1 - once at the MCU pin, once at their pull resistor). Ordinary KiCad practice and the netlist is unaffected, but a future harness run with bench_io absent would NOT raise single_global_label for those three nets; do not read their absence as proof of a connection.

Phantom-power path documented, not blocked: with the FC on and the emulator unpowered, the 14 device-side 10 k pull-ups on solar_emulation feed ~0.26 mA per line into 3V3_EMU through the RP2350 ESD diodes. Nothing is added in series (hard rule 6); U202's output stage and ~30 uF of bulk sink it. Confirm the reviewer accepts this rather than wanting a blocking element.

defects.title: Bench-window note quotes the 11.7 V LT3652 start-up threshold without allowing for the fuse + diode drop this sheet adds, so the stated 12 V low end will not start the charger
defects.evidence: Text at (20, 160) says "Bench PSU setting: 12 V to 18 V nominal ... Startup needs VIN >= VFLOAT + 3.3 V = 11.7 V". But the injection path the same sheet adds is F400 (Bourns MF-MSMF160/24X, Ri min 300 mΩ per the DigiKey parametric for MF-MSMF160/24X-2, R1 max 100 mΩ) in series with D400 (CDBA240LL-HF, VF ≈ 310 mV at 2 A per 01_brief_critique.md §13, so ≈ 0.25 V at 1.2 A). At the brief's ≤ 1.2 A expected bench draw the series drop is ≈ 0.37–0.60 V, so a terminal set to 12.0 V presents ≈ 11.4–11.6 V at VSOLAR — below the 11.7 V the note itself quotes.

defects.title: PTC Vmax (24 V) is set exactly equal to the sheet's own declared hard-maximum bench voltage, and its 1.6 A Ihold is a 23 °C rating carrying no stated derating margin against the 1.2 A expected draw
defects.evidence: F400/F401 note and Description: "1.60 A Ihold / 3.20 A Itrip / 24 V Vmax / 20 A Imax ... Vmax covers this sheet's 24 V hard-maximum bench PSU setting". PPTC Ihold is rated at 23 °C and derates with ambient (roughly 0.85× at 40 °C for this family), giving ≈ 1.36 A against the brief's ≤ 1.2 A expected draw.
defects.fix: Either state the hard-maximum bench setting as 20 V (still well over the 18 V nominal top and under 24 V with margin) and say so in the note, or pick a higher-Vmax PPTC / the brief's 2 A slow-blow ≥ 32 V alternative. Add the 23 °C Ihold basis and the derated figure to the note either way.

defects.title: Sheet lowers the brief-mandated bench-PSU hard maximum from 24 V to 20 V, justified by a false claim that the brief's 1.85 A polyfuse is not a procurable part
defects.evidence:
Brief §6.3 line 176 (and the approved fix text of critique item 6) mandates the note verbatim: "Text note giving the bench setting: supply **12–18 V, hard maximum 24 V**". The sheet text at (20 160), uuid 14e5c157, instead reads "Bench PSU setting: 12 V to 18 V nominal, HARD MAXIMUM 20 V (kept below F400/F401 24 V Vmax with margin ...)", and the F400/F401 note at (20 202.67) reinforces it with "do not raise the bench maximum above 20 V". The sole driver is the part choice: F400/F401 = Bourns MF-MSMF160/24X, Vmax 24 V (confirmed in the Bourns MF-MSMF datasheet Electrical Characteristics table: Vmax 24 V, Imax 20 A, Ihold 1.60 A, Itrip 3.20 A, Rmin 0.030 Ω, R1Max 0.100 Ω), which leaves zero margin at the brief's 24 V limit while tripped.

The report's justification is factually wrong on two counts. (a) It asserts the brief specified "1.85 A Ihold PTC, 30 V, 1812/4532"; grepping 00_pm_brief.md §6.3 line 175 and 01_brief_critique.md item 17 shows the brief says only "2 A slow or 1.85 A polyfuse" — no voltage, no package. (b) It asserts a 1.85 A PPTC "is not a real, procurable part"; that is true only inside the 1812 package the implementer imposed. Littelfuse 2920L185DR is real, stocked and LCSC-catalogued: verified live on jlcpcb.com/partdetail/Littelfuse-2920L185DR/C207086 → LCSC C207086, 2920 package, 1.85 A Ihold, 3.7 A Itrip, 33 V Vmax, Extended (also DigiKey 1211347 / F2871CT-ND, Arrow, Newark 18M4795). Within the Bourns MF-MSMF series itself the datasheet table confirms no part with Ihold ≥ 1.25 A exceeds 24 V, so the constraint is a property of the series the implementer picked, not of the market.

Net effect: a project-spec operating limit was narrowed on a schematic note without PM sign-off, and the integrator reading brief §6.3 against this sheet will find 24 V vs 20 V in conflict.
defects.fix: Re-spec F400/F401 to a fuse whose voltage rating supports the brief's mandated 24 V hard maximum, then restore the note text verbatim. Preferred: Littelfuse 2920L185DR — Value "1.85A_PTC_33V", Footprint `Fuse:Fuse_2920_7451Metric` (verified present in the KiCad 10 Fuse.pretty), Datasheet the Littelfuse 2920L page, `LCSC Part` = C207086 (live-verified, so rule 5 permits populating it — this also clears F400/F401 off the "needs LCSC" list), Description "PTC resettable fuse, Littelfuse 2920L185DR: 1.85 A Ihold / 3.7 A Itrip / 33 V Vmax / 40 A Imax". 33 V Vmax gives 9 V margin over the 24 V bench maximum. The brief's other sanctioned option (2 A slow-blow rated ≥32 V) is equally acceptable. Then change the text at uuid 14e5c157 back to "HARD MAXIMUM 24 V" with the brief's INA219-26 V / LT3652-32 V rationale, and delete the "do not raise above 20 V" sentence from the F400/F401 note at uuid 728b08b3. If the PM instead prefers to keep the Bourns part and the 20 V window, that needs an explicit PM decision recorded against brief §6.3, not a sheet-local self-correction.

defects.title: F400/F401 note quotes a derating figure from the wrong datasheet row and a PTC resistance 3x the datasheet maximum
defects.evidence: Sheet text at (20 200.67), uuid 56dc92d5: "typically ~0.85x for this family at 40 C ambient, i.e. ~1.36 A held". The Bourns MF-MSMF datasheet publishes an exact per-part Thermal Derating Table; the MF-MSMF160/24X row is -40/2.15, -20/2.00, 0/1.84, 23/1.60, 40/**1.31**, 50/1.13, 60/1.05, 70/0.81, 85/0.66 A. 1.36 A is the 40 °C figure for MF-MSMF160/**8X**, a different part in the same table. The true ratio is 1.31/1.60 = 0.82, and the real margin over the ≤1.2 A expected bench draw is 9 %, not the 13 % the note implies. Separately, the text at (20 164), uuid 97b1d055, states "F400/F401 (<=0.3 ohm)"; the datasheet gives Rmin 0.030 Ω and R1Max 0.100 Ω at 23 °C. The 0.3 Ω figure is conservative in the safe direction (it pushes the recommended bench setpoint up), so the note's ">=12.3 V (12.5 V recommended)" conclusion still holds, but the quoted number does not come from the datasheet.
defects.fix: Replace "typically ~0.85x for this family at 40 C ambient, i.e. ~1.36 A held" with the datasheet's own per-part value: "1.31 A at 40 C ambient per the MF-MSMF Thermal Derating Table". Replace "<=0.3 ohm" with the datasheet figure "R1max 0.100 ohm at 23 C" (or state explicitly that 0.3 Ω is an aged-resistance allowance, if that is the intent). If the fuse is re-spec'd per the major finding, restate both numbers from the replacement part's datasheet instead.

defects.title: VBAT_BENCH_N has no DC return when the bench PSU is unplugged — the replica has an indeterminate/bistable state and can put a permanent 4.2 mA drain on the FC net Dir_Chrg_In (and ~8.4 V on the J500 "B−" terminal)

Its only resistive connection is R504 (1 k) to the divider mid, i.e. 2 k to `Dir_Chrg_In` via R503; its only path to `B-` is Q500's channel in series with Q501's channel (Q501 is an N-ch IRF7458 with source on `B-`, so its body diode blocks the drain→B− direction — LCSC C10879 = IRF7458TRPBF N-channel). With J500 open and `Dir_Chrg_In` live (real pack on J14 per D11, or the LT3652), two self-consistent DC states exist: (i) VBAT_BENCH_N floats to ≈ Dir_Chrg_In through R503+R504, U500 sees VDD−VSS ≈ 0 V, both FETs stay off, and J500 pin 3 (silkscreened "B−") sits at ≈ +8.4 V w.r.t. board ground; (ii) if COUT/DOUT are already on (PSU just unplugged, or a fast Dir_Chrg_In rise held the node down through C503) the state latches with both FETs on and R503+R504 draw a permanent 4.2 mA from `Dir_Chrg_In` to `B-`. Report §8 open question 3 says the divider current flows "whenever the PSU is on", which is not the governing condition, and neither state is mentioned in the sheet notes.

Datasheet (Diodes 2N7002, DS11303 Rev 33-2, July 2013, 'Electrical Characteristics -> ON CHARACTERISTICS'): VGS(th) min 1.0 V, MAX 2.5 V at VDS=VGS, ID=250uA; lowest RDS(on) spec point is VGS=5.0 V (7.5 ohm max, ID=0.05 A); ID(ON) 0.5 A min is specified only at VGS=10 V. No on-state parameter is specified at or below VGS=2.72 V. VGS(th) has a negative tempco, so a cold bench raises it further.
Required sink current (tools/baseline/netlist.kicadxml): FC_RESET = J16.2, R1.2, SW2.A/A', TP2.1, U18.26 with R1 = 10k to +3V3 (RP2350.kicad_sch) -> ~330 uA to hold U18 RUN below VIL. A worst-case-threshold 2N7002 at 2.59-2.72 V VGS has 0.09-0.22 V of overdrive and is at/below its own 250 uA threshold-definition current, so FC_RESET would not be pulled below the RUN input threshold at all.

defects.title: SW703 uses a 2-pin SW_SPST symbol on a 3-pad SPDT footprint — pad 3 has no symbol pin, and this contradicts the reference design the report cites
defects.evidence: bench_io.kicad_sch lib_symbols `Switch:SW_SPST` defines exactly two pins ('1','2'); the netlist gives SW703.1 -> WDT_DISABLE and SW703.2 -> GND. The assigned footprint ~/Documents/KiCad/easyeda2kicad/easyeda2kicad.pretty/SW-TH_SHOU-HAN_SS12D10G4.kicad_mod lines 33-35 defines three thru_hole pads named 1, 2, 3 at x = -4.80 / 0.00 / +4.80 and no others, so pad 3 is left with no matching pin and no net when the PCB is updated from the schematic, and the schematic/PCB parity check will flag it. SS12D10G4 (LCSC C2887259, verified live on lcsc.com / jlcpcb.com) is an SPDT whose centre pin is the common pole, so pad 2 = common, pads 1 and 3 = the two throws; which throw is 'disabled' is also not stated anywhere on the sheet. The reference the brief cites and the report claims parity with does NOT do this: refs/upgraded/debug_board_v1/debug_board_v1.kicad_sch uses `(lib_id "Switch:SW_Push_SPDT")` (3 pins) at (260.35, 124.46) with the identical footprint. Report §2 Block D and §10 finding 5 assert '2 of the SPDT's 3 terminals are used, same as debug_board_v1' — that is not what debug_board_v1 does. No FC sheet uses Switch:SW_SPST at all (grep of FlatSat_V1/eps_side/load_switches/watchdog/RP2350 = 0 hits), so there is no heritage precedent either.
defects.fix: Either (a) change SW703 to a 3-pin symbol — `Switch:SW_SPDT` or `Switch:SW_Push_SPDT` as debug_board_v1 uses — with pin 2 (common) -> GND, pin 1 -> WDT_DISABLE and a `no_connect` marker on pin 3, or (b) keep `Switch:SW_SPST` and assign a genuinely 2-pad SPST footprint (e.g. Button_Switch_THT:SW_DIP_SPSTx01_Slide_9.78x4.72mm_W7.62mm_P2.54mm, as pyro_inhibit's SW600 does). Either way add a note saying which slider position grounds WDT_DISABLE. Re-run sch_lint and harness_erc afterwards.
